New OEM program wins and deepening wallet share with existing clients

BOE Varitronix partnership for optical bonding display systems from FY28

reports.summary: SJS Enterprises is positioned as a one-stop aesthetics platform champion, having successfully transformed from a 2W-centric decorative supplier into a diversified, design-led solutions provider with 25% market share in its segment. The company's structural growth levers include rising SUV penetration driving premium aesthetic content, capability-led inorganic expansion, and accelerating exports, with management targeting 18% revenue CAGR and margin expansion through FY28. Initiating coverage with BUY rating and Rs2,400 target price (19% upside) based on 30x FY28E PER, reflecting superior execution track record and sustainable competitive moat.
reports.connection_narrative: The automotive industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation centered on interior design and user experience as key brand differentiators, a structural shift driven by rising SUV penetration, increasing digitalization of cockpits, and consumer willingness to pay premium for sophisticated cabin aesthetics and smart interfaces. This premiumization trend is particularly pronounced in India where the SUV mix has risen from 26% in FY20 to 58% by FY26, directly expanding the content per vehicle opportunity from Rs1.2-1.5k to Rs3.5-5k for decorative and aesthetic components. Simultaneously, the shift toward touch-based interfaces and digital cockpit architectures is creating new TAM expansions in optical bonding, illuminated logos, and smart surface treatment technologies that represent structural whitespace opportunities for specialized suppliers. SJS Enterprises has positioned itself as the preeminent beneficiary of these themes through its strategic transformation from legacy 2W-focused decals and badges into an integrated aesthetics platform spanning printing and graphics, in-mold technologies, advanced optics, chrome plating, and emerging smart interface components. The company's acquisition of SJS Decoplast brought chrome-plating capabilities enabling deeper OEM integration and cross-selling within existing relationships, while Walter Pack India added advanced IMD/IML technologies and exposure to global tier-1 suppliers like Visteon and Continental, creating a pathway to participate in higher-value international automotive programs. Most critically, the company's recent technical license agreement with BOE Varitronix for optical display bonding systems opens a Rs30-40bn TAM opportunity from FY28 onward, positioning SJS at the intersection of interior design premium-ization and the digital cockpit architecture transformation. SJS's competitive edge stems from its 20+ year relationships with top 10 OEMs, proprietary design and engineering capabilities in aesthetics, and proven execution ability to scale acquisitions profitably—demonstrated by delivering 3x and 1.5x revenue multiples on Decoplast and WPI respectively since acquisition. The company has historically protected margins at 28-33% EBITDA despite raw material volatility through product refresh cycles that allow cost pass-through to OEMs every 12-15 months, and management targets margin expansion of 400-500bps through export scale-up to 14-15% of revenue by FY28. The single most important catalyst to monitor is the ramp-up of the new BOE Varitronix optical bonding display capabilities and corresponding commercial traction with global OEM programs, which could unlock step-function revenue growth and TAM expansion from FY28 onward. The primary risk to the thesis is execution risk on greenfield chrome plating and display system capacity additions, as well as potential compressed near-term margins if crude oil prices spike significantly, impacting raw material costs faster than OEMs refresh product specifications.

BIS norms implementation driving SS bottle sales; glassware import substitution opportunity with >80% of domestic demand via imports

catalysts: BIS norms implementation for stainless steel bottles
Ramp-up of glassware manufacturing facility (20k TPA plant in Rajasthan commissioned Mar-24)

reports.summary: Anand Rathi initiates coverage on Cello World with BUY rating and Rs500 target price (12-month). The company is a diversified consumer brand trading at an unjustified 21% discount to peers despite superior fundamentals, outperformance on revenue growth and margin resilience, and strong ROIC profile. Catalysts include BIS-driven SS bottle expansion, glassware import substitution, and successful Cello brand integration in writing instruments.
reports.connection_narrative: India's consumer discretionary sector is experiencing a structural shift driven by regulatory support and import substitution tailwinds. The implementation of BIS norms for stainless steel bottles is creating barriers for unorganized competitors while benefiting established branded players with manufacturing scale. Simultaneously, the glassware market faces over 80 percent import dependency, creating a compelling opportunity for organized domestic manufacturers to gain market share as consumers increasingly prefer certified, branded products over cheap Chinese imports. The broader shift from unbranded to branded consumerware reflects rising middle-class aspirations and improving retail infrastructure through modern trade and e-commerce channels. Cello World is uniquely positioned to capitalize on these trends given its established portfolio spanning consumerware, writing instruments, and moulded furniture, supported by a proven management team with six decades of industry experience. The company's recent acquisition of the Cello brand from BIC Cello in November 2025 positions it to recapture market share in writing instruments, now projected to grow at 28.1 percent CAGR. Its glassware facility in Rajasthan, operational since March 2024 with 20,000 TPA capacity, directly addresses import substitution dynamics with high-margin products. The consumerware core benefits from BIS normalization of SS bottles, where Cello has already established eight manufacturing lines with plans for two additional lines in FY27. Management's track record of scaling new businesses and diversified SKU offering (19,500 across categories) provides competitive moat against fragmented competition. The most critical near-term catalyst is the successful ramping of SS bottle production under new BIS norms, which could drive consumerware segment growth acceleration; however, raw material price volatility remains the primary risk that could compress margins if input costs spike without corresponding pricing power.
